subject: The interpretation of p-value in M2 statistics

messages.author: a29b76a7fee2ac43
messages.subject: The interpretation of p-value in M2 statistics
parts:
Hi all,

I am puzzled by the p-value of 0 in the M2 statistics, but it was p=1 in the G2. The RMSEA, TLI and CFI seem to suggest a good fit in M2, but the p-value is 0. Should I interpret this as model misfit because p-value is 0 regardless of RMSEA, CFI or TLI values? Thanks in advance.

messages.author: 08146071976f553f
messages.subject: Re: The interpretation of p-value in M2 statistics
parts:
Hello Zhao,

I struggled with the same question but this paper really helped al lot: 1. Maydeu-Olivares, A., & Joe, H. (2014). Assessing Approximate Fit in Categorical Data Analysis. Multivariate Behavioral Research, 49(4), 305–328. https://doi.org/10.1080/00273171.2014.911075

Cheers, Guido

messages.author: 08146071976f553f
messages.subject: Re: The interpretation of p-value in M2 statistics
parts: Glad I could help you. I cannot answer the question about Lavaan. In general, differences may be due to the complexity of the model or the number of variables in the model. Complex models with many variables can sometimes result in a good fit according to one metric, but a poor fit according to another. It is therefore important to consider multiple fit indices when evaluating model suitability, and not rely solely on a single index.
